items.title: Meet the winners of our Claude Opus 4.8 Build Day hackathon | Claude
items.summary_1line: From reconstructing Tang Dynasty architecture to polling a synthetic San Francisco, see what the winners of our latest hackathon built with Claude Opus 4.8 in a day.
items.editor_note: Adoption signal — Anthropic showcases hackathon winners who built with Opus 4.8 in a single day.

editorial.tldr: Anthropic shipped Claude Opus 4.8 on May 28, framing it in its own release note as "a modest but tangible improvement" on its predecessor — the line Simon Willison flagged as his favourite part of the announcement in his hands-on. The release landed in the same news cycle as Anthropic's $65B Series H raise (at a $965B valuation) and the Dynamic Workflows/ultracode launch. Three weeks later, Anthropic showcased what developers built on the model at an Opus 4.8 Build Day hackathon.
editorial.whats_new: The latest beat (Jun 17) shifts from launch coverage to adoption: Anthropic spotlighting the winners of an Opus 4.8 Build Day hackathon — projects ranging from reconstructing Tang Dynasty architecture to polling a synthetic San Francisco, each built with the model in a single day.
editorial.why_it_matters: Opus 4.8 is positioned as an incremental upgrade by Anthropic's own "modest but tangible" framing, so for platform engineers the migration case rests on marginal gains rather than a step change — while the Build Day projects signal what's now buildable on it in a day.
editorial.take_for_builders: Treat the move to Opus 4.8 as a marginal upgrade by Anthropic's own framing — weigh migration on incremental gains, not a step change.
